classification.difficultyReason: Reduce three geometric lengths to two variables using the perimeter, model both side relationships and interpret three exact lengths.

content.prompt: The triangle $ABC$ has a perimeter of $4\text{ m}$. Find the length of each side if $AB+BC=2AC$ and $AB+AC=3BC$.

answer.worked:
Let $AB=x$ metres and $BC=y$ metres. The perimeter gives $AC=4-x-y$ metres.

The two side relationships give
$$\begin{align*}x+y&=2(4-x-y)\\3x+3y&=8\end{align*}$$
and
$$\begin{align*}x+(4-x-y)&=3y\\4-y&=3y\\4&=4y\\y&=1.\end{align*}$$
Substitute $y=1$ into $3x+3y=8$:
$$\begin{align*}3x+3&=8\\3x&=5\\x&=\frac{5}{3}.\end{align*}$$
Then
$$\begin{align*}AC&=4-\frac{5}{3}-1\\AC&=\frac{4}{3}\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
Thus $AB=\frac{5}{3}\text{ m}$, $BC=1\text{ m}$ and $AC=\frac{4}{3}\text{ m}$.

Check: the perimeter is $\frac{5}{3}+1+\frac{4}{3}=4$ metres; $AB+BC=\frac{8}{3}=2AC$ and $AB+AC=3=3BC$.
